plan_a_advantages: Includes longer, dedicated aerobic runs (86 and 104 minutes) to build endurance.
More structured progression of run durations, gradually increasing the workload.
Explicitly targets trail-specific durability with the longer runs.
plan_b_advantages: More rest days (2 vs. 1), potentially beneficial for recovery and preventing overtraining.
Incorporates some hill work, which is a valuable component of trail running training.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes building a solid aerobic base through longer, sustained runs at an easy pace, which is crucial for trail running's demands. Plan B, conversely, focuses almost entirely on easy runs with minimal variation and no dedicated longer efforts, potentially hindering the development of the endurance needed for longer trail races. While Plan B includes some hill work, it lacks the consistent, extended aerobic stimulus that Plan A provides.
